title: Three-Phase BLDC Motor Controller
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: a three-phase gate driver, an MCU with motor-control timers

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board includes an MCU that has motor-control timers.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: an MCU with motor-control timers, phase/bus current sensing

fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: provide substantial copper for the phase/bus current

fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: keep current-sense routing Kelvin and away from switching nodes

fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: and provide a plausible thermal path

fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Connectors for DC power and motor phases should sit near the power stage.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Logic and communications should occupy a quieter region of the board. The brief states this as a should, not as one of its must clauses.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Logic and communications should occupy a quieter region of the board.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The repository should remain a consumer of the shared PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest toolkit rather than accumulating board-specific logic in the toolkit.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: The repository should remain a consumer of the shared `PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest` toolkit rather than accumulating board-specific logic in the toolkit.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Stated requirements are authoritative; where the brief leaves a choice open, the design agent must make and document a reasonable engineering decision rather than invent a hidden user requirement.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Treat stated requirements as authoritative; where the brief leaves choices open, make and document reasonable engineering decisions rather than inventing hidden user requirements.

open_decisions.decision: Selection of the six N-channel MOSFETs: voltage and current rating, package, RDS(on) versus gate-charge trade-off, and avalanche/SOA margin.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes only the count, type and external placement of the switches; it names no device, package or rating.

open_decisions.decision: Selection of the three-phase gate driver and the drive architecture around it (bootstrap versus separately supplied high side, integrated versus external dead-time control, which built-in protection features are relied on, and how many distinct gate-drive loops the chosen scheme creates).
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "a three-phase gate driver" and says nothing about its supply scheme, features or part.

open_decisions.decision: Gate-drive parameters: gate drive impedance and any gate resistor values, turn-on/turn-off asymmetry, dead time, and any gate clamping or pull-down for safe start-up.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief constrains the physical loop but states no switching or gate-drive numbers.

open_decisions.decision: MCU selection: family, core, package, memory, peripheral count, and debug/programming interface.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires only "an MCU with motor-control timers" and names no device or vendor.

open_decisions.decision: Current-sense topology: shunt versus magnetic sensing, low-side versus in-line/high-side placement, how many phases are individually sensed, whether phase and bus current are measured by separate chains or derived from a shared one, sense element value and power rating, and the amplifier or integrated sensor used.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief mandates "phase/bus current sensing" and a Kelvin routing rule, but not the sensing method, placement or channel count, and does not expand its own phase/bus shorthand.

open_decisions.decision: DC bus voltage sense implementation: attenuation method and ratio, filtering, ADC scaling and any protection on that node.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires DC bus voltage sensing but specifies no measurement range, accuracy or implementation.

open_decisions.decision: Encoder and Hall interface details: whether both are populated simultaneously or treated as alternatives, connector, sensor supply and its current budget, single-ended versus differential encoder support, level shifting, input filtering and protection, and channel count.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names "encoder/Hall inputs" as a requirement without defining the electrical interface or resolving whether its slash means both together or either one.

open_decisions.decision: CAN-FD implementation: transceiver choice, bit rates, termination strategy, bus connector, common-mode/ESD protection, and whether isolation is used.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names the interface only; it states no data rate, connector, topology or isolation requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Auxiliary rail generation: how logic, analog and gate-drive supplies are derived from the 24 V bus, their voltages, topology (switching versus linear), sequencing and current budget.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on internal rails; it fixes only the 24 V bus.

open_decisions.decision: DC-link and decoupling capacitance: bulk capacitance value and technology, ripple-current budget, and placement relative to the half-bridges.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief demands compact commutation loops but states no capacitance, ripple or ESR requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Protection strategy: overcurrent and short-circuit response and its speed, reverse-polarity protection, overvoltage/regeneration handling, fault latching and recovery, and any thermal shutdown.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief specifies sensing but names no protection function, threshold or response behaviour.

open_decisions.decision: Commutation and control scheme (trapezoidal, sinusoidal or field-oriented), PWM/modulation scheme and switching frequency, and the extent of firmware in scope.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief specifies motor-control timers and position-feedback inputs but not the control algorithm, modulation scheme or switching frequency.

open_decisions.decision: Thermal path implementation: which devices the path is built for, copper area and weight devoted to them, thermal via pattern, whether a heatsink or chassis coupling is used, airflow assumption, ambient range and allowed temperature rise.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief asks for "a plausible thermal path" without naming what it serves, and leaves every quantitative thermal target and mechanism unstated.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, mounting-hole pattern, keep-outs and any enclosure or heatsink mechanical interface.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief gives placement preferences but no dimensions, shape or mechanical envelope.

open_decisions.decision: Stackup detail: whether the metadata's likely 4 layers is adopted, copper weights, dielectric thicknesses and plane assignment.
open_decisions.why_open: The layer count is a benchmark metadata hint, not a stated requirement, and the brief fixes no copper weight or stackup.

open_decisions.decision: Connector selection for DC power, motor phases, encoder/Hall and CAN: type, current and temperature rating, orientation and part numbers.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief expresses only a preference for where the DC power and motor-phase connectors sit, not what they are.

open_decisions.decision: Grounding and return strategy: partitioning of power return, gate-drive return, analog sense return and logic ground, plane splits, and the star or single-point connection.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires Kelvin sensing and prefers a quiet logic region but does not define the ground architecture that achieves them.

open_decisions.decision: Input EMI filtering and switching-noise containment on the 24 V input and motor phases, and any snubbing at the half-bridges.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on EMC targets, filtering and snubbers.

open_decisions.decision: Test, bring-up and calibration provisions: test points, programming interface, status indicators, current-sense calibration method and safe low-power bring-up path.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no test or manufacturing-test requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Fabrication and assembly targets: fabricator capability class, single- versus double-sided assembly, minimum trace/space and via rules adopted, and which current-capacity standard is cited to justify them.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no fabricator, process, standard or manufacturability constraint.
